title: Section C practice task bank (teacher-written titles, pupil PDF)
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lessons 25, 42 (Section C practice task bank (teacher-written titles, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 25: Section C: choosing your task from three. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Three tasks (practice set)
points: (a) 'Young people spend too much time indoors.' Discuss.
(b) Write a story with the title 'The Storm'.
(c) Describe a busy place as it closes for the night.

head: Question
Why it matters
rows: Can I plan it in five minutes?
Do I know the form well?
form, audience and register earn AO4
Can I show varied vocabulary and sentences?

parts.text: (a): ideas come, but I need both sides and a judgement
(b): a storm story risks a big plot; I would make it one room, one night
(c): one place, a clear shift from busy to empty: perfect for CLOSER
Decision: (c), because I can plan it fastest and show range

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Choice made in under two minutes, with a reason.

keywords.def: the type of writing: story, description, essay
why it is written: to describe, narrate, discuss

questions.q: Choose a task from the practice set and write your two-minute reason.
questions.a: A choice with a reason linked to planning and form.

questions.q: Identify form, audience and purpose for task (a).
questions.a: Form: discursive essay; audience: general reader or examiner; purpose: to explore both sides and judge.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, plan all three tasks in three minutes each (a five-line plan for each). Starter: '(a) thesis: ...'
questions.a: Three five-line plans showing the different shapes: discursive, narrative, descriptive.

questions.q: Extend: circle the plan you could write best and say why.
Stretch: write the first sentence for each task.
Which is the best reason to choose a task?
options: I can plan it quickly and control its form
questions.a: A) I can plan it quickly and control its form. Planning speed and control of form win marks.

questions.q: The first question to ask is...
questions.a: A) can I plan it in five minutes?
options: can I plan it in five minutes?

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: The one I can plan fastest and control best, even if another seems more fun.
